**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, assignment).**

- **Issue:** Section 20(d) (p0142) imposes a flat mutual bar on assignment without the other party's written consent — no affiliate carve-out, no M&A/successor carve-out, and no "not unreasonably withheld" standard. Section 3(c) (p0033) compounds this one-sidedly, barring Sparkling from assigning except as authorised by Garman in writing, and Section 2 grants only a "non-transferable" licence. This fails the fallback position (successor assignment on written notice with a reasonableness standard) and would block a Sparkling reorganisation or sale.
- **Good news:** Section 17's termination triggers contain no change-of-control right for Garman, and no re-pricing trigger exists anywhere in the document.
- **Redline (validated, preferred position):** Sparkling may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition, reorganisation or sale of substantially all assets on written notice; Garman may assign only with our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a Sparkling competitor; residual consents subject to a reasonableness standard; express confirmation that our change of control gives Garman no termination, suspension or re-pricing right. Section 3(c) conformed with an "except as permitted by Section 20(d)" opener.
